chapterName: Linear Equations, Coordinate Geometry & Linear Programming
questionText:
A manufacturing firm produces two products, $X$ and $Y$. The contribution margin function is given by:

$$Z = 45X + 60Y$$

Subject to the resource constraints:
1. $3X + 4Y \le 240$ (Machine hours)
2. $2X + Y \le 110$ (Skilled labor hours)
3. $X \ge 0, \; Y \ge 0$

At which corner point $(X, Y)$ of the feasible region is the total contribution $Z$ maximized, and what is the maximum contribution?

options.text: Both (0, 60) and (40, 30) yield the maximum Z = Rs. 3,600

questionText:
The total cost function $C(q)$ and total revenue function $R(q)$ of an electronics manufacturer for output $q$ units are:

$$C(q) = 180,000 + 420q$$
$$R(q) = 900q - 0.06q^2$$

What is the **profit-maximizing output level** $q^*$ and the maximum profit earned?

An investor deposits **Rs. 50,000** at the end of every quarter into a sinking fund that earns **12% per annum compounded quarterly**. Using the ordinary annuity formula:

$$FV = PMT \times \left[ \frac{(1 + i)^n - 1}{i} \right]$$

What will be the accumulated value of the fund at the end of **5 years** (rounded to the nearest rupee)?

A capital project requires an initial outlay of **Rs. 2,350,000** at $t = 0$. The expected net cash inflows are summarized below:

| Year ($t$) | Net Cash Inflow (Rs.) | Discount Factor at 14% | Discount Factor at 18% |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Year 1 | 900,000 | 0.8772 | 0.8475 |
| Year 2 | 1,100,000 | 0.7695 | 0.7182 |
| Year 3 | 1,200,000 | 0.6750 | 0.6086 |

Using linear interpolation, what is the approximate **Internal Rate of Return (IRR)** of the project?

For a sample of $n = 10$ observations, the mean was calculated as $\bar{x} = 42$ and the standard deviation as $s = 6$ (using divisor $n$). Later it was discovered that one observation was wrongly recorded as **$34$** instead of the correct value **$54$**.

What is the **corrected mean** ($\bar{x}_{\text{new}}$)?

Two investment portfolios have the following return statistics:

| Portfolio | Mean Return (%) | Standard Deviation (%) |
| :--- | ---: | ---: |
| Portfolio Alpha | 15.0% | 3.0% |
| Portfolio Beta | 20.0% | 5.0% |

Using the **Coefficient of Variation** ($CV = \frac{\sigma}{\mu} \times 100\%$), which statement is true?

options.text: Portfolio Alpha is more consistent (CV = 20%) than Portfolio Beta (CV = 25%)
Portfolio Beta is more consistent (CV = 20%) than Portfolio Alpha (CV = 25%)
Both portfolios have identical relative dispersion (CV = 22.5%)
Portfolio Alpha has CV = 60% and Portfolio Beta has CV = 125%

questionText:
From a dataset of $n = 8$ monthly production runs, the following summary statistics were obtained for Output ($x$, in '000 units) and Factory Overheads ($y$, in Rs. '000):

$$\sum x = 40, \quad \sum y = 200, \quad \sum xy = 1,120, \quad \sum x^2 = 240$$

Using the least squares formula $b = \frac{n\sum xy - (\sum x)(\sum y)}{n\sum x^2 - (\sum x)^2}$, what is the fitted linear regression equation $\hat{y} = a + bx$?

An internal audit reveals that **$5\%$** of vouchers processed manually contain a coding error. If an auditor selects a random sample of **$n = 4$** vouchers independently, what is the binomial probability that **at least one** voucher contains an error?

$$P(X = x) = \binom{n}{x} p^x (1 - p)^{n - x}$$

The lifetimes of industrial LED bulbs follow a Normal distribution with mean $\mu = 1,200\text{ hours}$ and standard deviation $\sigma = 80\text{ hours}$. Given that $P(0 \le Z \le 1.50) = 0.4332$ and $P(0 \le Z \le 2.00) = 0.4772$, what percentage of bulbs last **between $1,080$ hours and $1,360$ hours**?
